security_audit.summary: Most external command findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences and inline model IDs, not Ruby backtick execution. The remote installer piped to sh is a confirmed critical risk, and the related network URL is confirmed high risk. Other URLs are documentation links or placeholder media examples with no evidence of secret exfiltration.

remediation.suggestion: Replace curl-to-sh installation with a package manager, checksum-verified download, or separate reviewable install steps.
State clearly that media URLs and generation requests are sent to inference.sh apps for processing.
Move related skill install commands to documentation and tell users to review each skill before installing it.

content.user_title: Create AI Avatar Videos with Inference.sh
content.value_statement: Teams need presenter videos without full video production. This skill guides avatar, lipsync, and dubbing workflows through the inference.sh CLI.
actual_capabilities: Shows how to install and log in to the inference.sh CLI.
Lists OmniHuman, Fabric, PixVerse, and LatentSync choices for avatar video tasks.
Provides CLI examples for image-and-audio avatar generation.
Outlines a text-to-speech to avatar video workflow.
Outlines a transcription, translation, and lipsync workflow for dubbing.
Links to inference.sh documentation for app runs and streaming results.
limitations: Requires an inference.sh account, CLI access, and network connectivity.
Sends media URLs and generation requests to external inference.sh apps.
Output quality depends on source image, audio quality, and model limits.
Does not manage consent, likeness rights, or publication approvals.

use_cases.title: Produce Presenter Demos
use_cases.description: Create product demo videos from a presenter image and approved narration audio.

use_cases.title: Create Course Explainers
use_cases.description: Turn lessons into talking head videos for online training and educational content.

use_cases.title: Localize Existing Videos
use_cases.description: Plan transcription, translation, speech generation, and lipsync steps for multilingual releases.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Simple Avatar
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner avatar generation from prepared media.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to create an avatar video from my portrait URL and speech audio URL. Recommend the best model and command.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Model Options
prompt_templates.scenario: Choose a model for quality, speed, or source media.
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare OmniHuman, Fabric, and PixVerse for my talking head video. Explain which one fits my image, audio, and realism goals.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Dubbing Workflow
prompt_templates.scenario: Localize a video with translated speech and synced lips.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me dub an existing video into another language. Outline the inference.sh steps for transcription, translated speech, and lipsync.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Production Pipeline
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow with quality checks and repeatable steps.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a repeatable avatar video pipeline for multiple scripts. Include model selection, media preparation, review checkpoints, and final delivery steps.

output_examples.input: Create a product demo avatar from a presenter photo and narration file.
output_examples.output: Recommended OmniHuman 1.5 for high quality presenter video, with a short workflow for media checks, generation, and review.

output_examples.input: Localize this training video into Spanish with synced speech.
output_examples.output: Suggested workflow: transcribe the original audio, translate the script, generate Spanish speech, then apply lipsync to the source video.

output_examples.input: Choose between Fabric and PixVerse for a social media talking head.
output_examples.output: PixVerse is suggested for realistic lipsync, while Fabric is better for simple image-to-talking-video tasks.

best_practices: Use only images, voices, and scripts that you have permission to use.
Start with front-facing images and clean narration audio for stronger results.
Review generated videos for identity, pronunciation, and brand accuracy before publishing.
anti_patterns: Do not create videos that impersonate real people without clear consent.
Do not publish generated avatars without checking rights, disclosures, and local rules.
Do not use low quality or noisy source media for production results.

faq.question: What does this skill help create?
faq.answer: It helps create AI avatar, talking head, lipsync, and dubbing videos through inference.sh CLI workflows.

faq.question: Which models does it reference?
faq.answer: It references OmniHuman 1.5, OmniHuman 1.0, Fabric 1.0, PixVerse Lipsync, and LatentSync.

faq.question: Do I need an inference.sh account?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflow expects the inference.sh CLI, login, and access to the selected apps.

faq.question: Can it generate the script or voice?
faq.answer: It can guide a text-to-speech step, but scripts and translations still need review.

faq.question: Can I use real people as avatars?
faq.answer: Use real people only with permission and follow consent, disclosure, and rights requirements.

faq.question: Does it work with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report marks support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code compatible skill clients.
